feature: Math.heading(input: string): string is a bespoke (invented) built-in added under the Math namespace, so the static type checker treats it as `any` and no TypeSystem change is needed. It is implemented as a 3-helper pipeline: HNormalize -> HTitleCase -> HFinish.
contract: 1. Trim; collapse internal whitespace runs to a single space; split into words on spaces.
2. Title-case each word: first letter upper, rest lower.
3. SMALL-WORD rule: the words {a, an, the, of, and, or, in, on, to, for} are fully lowercased EXCEPT when the word is the FIRST or LAST word of the heading (those are always title-cased).
4. ACRONYM rule: a word that is ALL UPPERCASE in the input AND has length <= 4 (e.g. API, SQL, HTML, JSON, USA) is preserved verbatim (not title-cased, not small-word-lowered).
5. FINISH rule: strip any run of trailing punctuation chars (one or more of '.', ',', ';', ':', '!') from the final joined string.

BUG_A_titlecase_small_word_last.effect: The small-word rule exempts the FIRST word but not the LAST word, so a heading ending in a small word ({a, an, the, of, and, or, in, on, to, for}) wrongly lowercases that final word.

BUG_B_acronym_length.effect: The acronym length check uses >= 4 instead of > 4, so 4-letter all-caps acronyms like HTML and JSON are NOT recognized as acronyms and get title-cased to Html / Json. Acronyms of length <= 3 (API, SQL, CSS) are unaffected.

BUG_C_finish_trailing_punct_run.effect: Only ONE trailing punctuation char is stripped instead of the whole run, so 'Hello World!!' -> 'Hello World!', 'Notes on Design...' -> 'Notes on Design..', 'Wait for It.,' -> 'Wait for It.'.

h1.input: what it is all about the
h1.correct: What It Is All About The
h1.broken: What It Is All About the

h3.input: this is the end of the road to
h3.correct: This Is the End of the Road To
h3.broken: This Is the End of the Road to

h5.area: BUG B (HTML 4-letter; CSS 3-letter control inside same input)

h11.area: control (first/last not small words, no acronym, no punct)
